Edward William Judson (July20, 1931January31, 2026) was an American real estate executive, developer and investor.
Early life and education
Judson was born in New York City to Henry and Beatrice (née Horowitz) Judson. Henry Judson owned two seats on the New York Stock Exchange. The younger Judson attended Governor Dummer Academy in Massachusetts for high school. He then attended Harvard College, graduating magna cum laude with a BA in economics in 1953.
Career
Judson worked on Wall Street as a securities analyst until 1958 before taking a job with Oppenheimer Industries, which managed the investments of Jules Stein, founder of MCA Inc. He was soon placed in charge of Oppenheimer’s eastern real estate operations.
In 1972, he acquired these assets from Oppenheimer and reorganized them as Judson Realty, Inc. He subsequently played a key role in redeveloping Madison Avenue as a high-end retail corridor. The company closed leasing deals on Madison Avenue for some of the world’s best-known luxury retailers, including La Perla, Issey Miyake, LeSportsac, Vera Wang, agnès b., Wolford, Fauchon, J.Crew, Stuart Weitzman and Richemont.
In 1980, Judson developed the American Stanhope Hotel on Fifth Avenue, converting it from an apartment hotel. In 1981, he purchased the residential Hyde Park Hotel at Madison Avenue and 77th Street and redeveloped it into the Mark Hotel.
He created the Judson Art Warehouse in Long Island City in 1985. In 1993, he founded [https://masterpak-usa.com Masterpak, Inc.], a provider of archival art storage and shipping material supplies. He was a founding board member of the P.S. 1 Contemporary Art Center.
In 1996, Judson led the formation of the [https://madisonavenuebid.org Madison Avenue Business Improvement District], of which he served as chairperson until his death.
Personal life
Judson’s first and second marriages, to Denise Kline and Consuelo Vanderbilt Russell, ended in divorce. He was married to his third wife, Nina Bushkin Judson, at the time of his death. He had six sons by his first two marriages.
